_about: Supplemental map for src/Tools/apidocs/generate_rest_api.py and generate_postman.py. OpenAPI carries no response schemas, so each route's response type, status codes, and notes live here. tags orders and describes the folders and sections. bodies holds an example request body per schema (Postman variables in {{braces}}). examples holds response examples per type. samples gives the values the Markdown shows for each {{variable}}. pathVariables names the Postman variable for a path parameter where the default rule (topics/{id} gives topicId) does not fit. parameters notes query values. captures, postmanQuery, variableDefaults, and lastInFolder shape the Postman collection. tags.Health: An anonymous liveness and readiness probe. Container healthchecks and load balancers call it.
tags.Server: Public client configuration that the dashboard and mobile app read before anyone signs in: feature flags, the minimum app version, legal links, and the MCP URL.
tags.Token: Sessions. POST /v1.0/token exchanges login headers (an email and password, or an access key and secret) for a bearer token. The other routes validate, describe, refresh, and revoke the token you already hold.
tags.Profile: The signed-in user's own profile and password. Any authenticated user may call these for themselves.
tags.Tenants: Control plane. Tenants isolate every record in the system. Global administrators manage all tenants; tenant administrators can read their own.
tags.Users: Control plane. Users inside a tenant, with their administrator flags. Passwords are write-only.
tags.Credentials: Control plane. Access keys for programs. The secret is returned once, when the credential is created. The auth mode decides how a credential may be used: direct headers, signed requests, session exchange, or a mix.
tags.Roles: Control plane. Built-in and tenant-defined roles. A role is a named set of permissions.
tags.Permissions: Control plane. Permissions (resource types and operations, permit or deny) and the effective permissions a user or credential ends up with.
tags.Assignments: Control plane. Role assignments for users and scope assignments for credentials, at tenant or resource scope.
tags.Audit: Security and administration events: sign-ins, denials, credential use, settings changes, vault reveals.
tags.Request History: Captured REST requests with headers and bodies, for troubleshooting. Retention is set by RequestHistory.RetentionDays.
tags.Settings: Server settings. Secrets come back masked as ******** and a masked or empty secret is left unchanged on update. Some settings take effect only after a restart.
tags.Vault: Encrypted storage for API keys and tokens that model endpoints, search providers, and voices use. Lists and reads never include the secret; reveal is rate limited and audited.
tags.Models: Model endpoints (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and compatible servers), task role assignments, and the accounting record of every model call.
tags.Usage: Model usage and cost, grouped or bucketed over time. Members see their own; administrators can see the tenant, and global administrators every tenant.
tags.Devices: Push notification devices registered by the mobile app for the signed-in user.
tags.Topics: The things a reader follows. A topic has a research brief, weighted dimensions, constraints (keywords, domains, feeds, tracked questions), and email recipients.
tags.Refinement: The topic wizard. A session proposes dimensions, asks clarifying questions, drafts the brief and constraints, suggests sources, and then applies the topic. Generating steps call the configured model.
tags.Requests: One-time research requests: a report, podcast, or email summary produced once, now or at a set time. A request can later become a recurring topic.
tags.Schedules: When topics, editions, and requests run. Interval, days-of-week, days-of-month, one-time, and cron schedules, each in a time zone. Preview validates a schedule and lists its next runs.
tags.Runs: Research runs and their stages, search queries, search results, and model calls. A run can be watched live over server-sent events, canceled, or retried from a later stage.
tags.Search: Search providers (SearXNG, Tavily, You.com, RSS, Hacker News, arXiv, hosted model web search), per-topic provider choices, and test tools for queries and page fetches.
tags.Findings: Ranked results from runs, each backed by evidence. Findings can be pinned or hidden.
tags.Sources: Pages the pipeline fetched for your topics, with their extracted text.
tags.Predictions: Forecasts the pipeline extracted, with confidence and a horizon. They are resolved by hand or by accepting a proposed review.
tags.Suggestions: Things worth digging into next, with a status you move through (accept, snooze, dismiss, done).
tags.Briefings: Composed briefings with sections and items, their Markdown and HTML files, pinning past retention, and regeneration.
tags.Artifacts: Stored files: briefing Markdown and HTML, audio, and exports. Content streams with Range support.
tags.Editions: Recurring briefings that gather several topics, with a template, audio and email switches, and a lookback window.
tags.Templates: Briefing templates in Markdown. Every save is a version; templates can be validated, previewed, rolled back, reset, imported, and exported.
tags.Media: Audio episodes made from briefings, with chapters.
tags.Voices: Text-to-speech voice profiles, with a test route that speaks a sample.
tags.Podcast feeds: Private podcast feed tokens. The feed URL embeds the secret, which is shown once.
tags.Email: The email outbox, test and preview sends, resends, and the signed-in user's email preferences.
tags.Feedback: Ratings and reasons on findings, predictions, suggestions, sources, domains, and briefings. Feedback drives learning and analytics.
tags.Learning: Preferences learned from feedback (or written by hand), their review flow, and ranking weight recommendations.
tags.Analytics: Reports over relevance, accuracy, feedback, suggestions, reasons, quality, email, and runs. Defaults to the caller's data for the last 90 days.
tags.Prompts: Prompt templates by key and scope, topic overrides, version history, rollback, reset, and the prompt lab.
tags.Promotional codes: Global administrators create, generate, and manage promotional codes that grant plans.
tags.Plans: Global administrators manage plans, their entitlement values, and per-user plan assignments.
tags.Account: Sign-up, email verification, password reset, the signed-in user's plan, usage meter, data export, account deletion, and promotional code redemption.
tags.Public: Routes reached from emails and podcast apps. They take no session; a token in the path is the credential. Feedback and unsubscribe pages are HTML forms.
tags.OpenAPI: The OpenAPI 3 document and Swagger UI that Watson serves. They are not tagged in the document itself.
tags.MCP servers: Remote MCP tool servers that agentic research may call, their discovered tools, and the per-tool allow-list.

parameters.all: Administrators: true for the whole tenant instead of one user.
parameters.allTenants: Global administrators: true for every tenant.
parameters.authorizationResult: Authorization outcome, for example Permitted or Denied.
parameters.batchId: Codes made by one generate call.
parameters.bucketMinutes: Bucket width in minutes for time series.
parameters.dimensionId: Only findings matched to this dimension.
parameters.disposition: What the pipeline did with each result.
parameters.download: true sends the file as an attachment.
parameters.dryRun: true runs without sending email or counting in history.
parameters.force: true also revokes and removes redemptions (for test codes).
parameters.fromStage: Rerun from this stage: Synthesize, ReviewPredictions, Predict, Suggest, ComposeBriefing, or Notify. Omit for a fresh run.
parameters.includeBelowThreshold: Include findings under the display threshold.
parameters.includeHistory: Include superseded ratings, not only the current one.
parameters.isCustomized: Only prompts changed from the shipped default.
parameters.isOneTime: Only one-time request topics (true) or recurring topics (false).
parameters.mine: Administrators: true lists only your own records.
parameters.minScore: Lowest final score to include (0 to 100).
parameters.modelEndpointId: Only calls to this model endpoint.
parameters.origin: Distilled from feedback, or written by a user.
parameters.ownerId: The topic, edition, or request the schedule belongs to.
parameters.planId: Only codes that grant this plan.
parameters.promptKey: Only calls made with this prompt key.
parameters.purge: true deletes an already revoked token.
parameters.refinementSessionId: Only calls made by this refinement session.
parameters.statusClass: `2xx`, `4xx`, `5xx`, and so on; sets the minimum and maximum status code.
parameters.tenantId: Global administrators: another tenant. Ignored for everyone else.
parameters.tenantOnly: Only tenant-level prompts, not topic overrides.
parameters.tier: Finding tier. BelowThreshold also returns below-threshold findings.
parameters.to: End of the window (UTC). Default now.
parameters.top: Most rows to return. Default 50, maximum 1000.
parameters.userId: Administrators: another user's records. Ignored for members.
parameters.a: Action to preselect, from the email link.

GET /v1.0/api/briefings/{id}/download.notes: Query `format` is `md` (default) or `html`. The file is sent as an attachment and honors `Range`.

GET /v1.0/api/artifacts/{id}/content.notes: Streams the stored file with its own content type. Pass `download=true` for an attachment. Honors `Range`.

status.200: The token was already registered; the existing device is returned

GET /v1.0/public/feedback/{token}.notes: Renders the one-click feedback page from an email link. The optional `a` query value preselects an action.

POST /v1.0/public/feedback/{token}.notes: Form post (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) from the feedback page.

POST /v1.0/public/unsubscribe/{token}.notes: Form post (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) from the unsubscribe page.

status.503: The database is unreachable; the body still describes each component.

POST /v1.0/api/topics/{id}/learn.notes: Runs the learning pass at once and returns how many preferences it proposed plus the topic's preferences.

GET /v1.0/api/analytics/runs.notes: Dry runs are excluded and days are gap-filled. Sources examined are the Search stage's items out, fetched are the Fetch stage's items out, and used are the distinct sources behind a non-duplicate finding at or above the display threshold. Provider yield is the share of a provider's results whose source produced such a finding in the same run. Stage percentiles interpolate linearly over finished (succeeded or failed) stage rows.

status.202: Accepted (the body is an ErrorResponse-shaped notice with error Accepted)

status.409: The email matches accounts in several tenants; the body is a TenantSelectionResponse. Sign in again with x-tenant-guid.

GET /openapi.json.notes: The OpenAPI 3 document this reference is generated from.

status.202: Accepted (same body whether or not the email has an account)

status.400: BadRequest (weak password, or expired, used, or unknown link)

status.200: OK (success false with the error when the server cannot be reached)
